html:
The Mozambican War of Independence was fought from September 1964 to 1974 by FRELIMO's guerrillas against Portuguese rule, mainly in the far north and later in Tete province.

Operating from Tanzania, FRELIMO built liberated zones on the Makonde plateau. Portugal answered with a large army, resettlement villages and massacres such as Wiriyamu in 1972, while building the Cahora Bassa Dam in the war zone.

The war, with those in Angola and Guinea-Bissau, drained Portugal and led to the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon in April 1974. The Lusaka Accord of September 1974 handed power to FRELIMO, and Mozambique became independent on 25 June 1975 under Samora Machel.
sum: The Mozambican War of Independence was fought from September 1964 to 1974 by FRELIMO's guerrillas against Portuguese rule, mainly in the far north and later in Tete province.
